column1: # TITLE: Identification of differentially expressed miRNAs in BM+ vs. BM- lung cancer samples

# SUMMARY: Brain metastasis (BM) can affect up to 25% of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients during their lifetime. Efforts to characterize patients that will develop BM have been fairly disappointing. Small non-coding microRNAs (miRNAs) regulate the expression of target mRNAs by repressing their translation or regulating their sequence-specific degradation. miRNAs play a role in regulating a variety of targets and
column4: which makes them a powerful tool to be exploited for early detection of disease
column7: we investigated miRNAs that may serve as biomarkers to differentiate between NSCLC patients with and without BM. miRNA microarray profiling was performed on samples from clinically matched NSCLC from patients with BM (BM+) and without BM (BM-). miR-328 and miR-330-3p were able to correctly classify BM+ vs. BM- patients. Gene expression analysis comparing NSCLC parental and stably transfected miR-328 cells identified several significantly differentially-expressed genes
column8: whose expression may be directly or indirectly regulated by miR-328.
